Scope note: This execution covers the Login form (authentication, field validation, boundary/negative/special-character inputs, session-guard security check, basic accessibility), the Contact module reached after selecting branch NEYVELI CAO (list/search, New Contact form for Individual & Business Entity, address management, field-level validation, KYC business-rule enforcement, and security checks), the Contact Detail/Roles module (Employee, Referral, Party, Advocate, Subscriber, Guarantor and Related Parties — every field across Salary Info, Personal Details, General Information, Family Details, Education and Previous Experience/Transfer History was verified present, with mandatory-field, boundary and XSS checks executed), and the Group Formation module (field coverage, mandatory-field validation, Chit Value/Chit Period dropdown behavior, boundary/format checks, XSS safety, and Auction Date/Week and Bid Amount toggles) — all executed live against the running application using Playwright (Chromium). Other application modules were not in scope for this run.

Known CRUD coverage gap (by design, not an oversight): On both the Contact module and the Group Formation module, the full CRUD scenario set required by the test methodology (Successful Create → Read/Search → Update → Delete → Duplicate-data check) could not be completed, because in both cases the application's own Save action never succeeds: Contact's Save Contact is a silent no-op after using "+ Add" on Address/KYC (see BUG-006), and Group Formation's Save is blocked by a stale "Chit Period Required" validator even when Chit Period holds a valid selection (see BUG-007). Per test-data safety rules, no dummy/test record was ever force-persisted to work around these blockers — the Create flow was exercised up to the exact point where each defect blocks the save (see TC_CONTACT_013 and TC_GF_CREATE01), and Update/Delete/Duplicate/Read-back testing on these two modules remains blocked until the respective defect is fixed by the development team. The 311,484-record production Contact database was never written to as a result.

TC_CONTACT_017 Save Contact after adding an Address and a KYC document via '+ Add' actually creates the contact record CRUD / Root Cause Analysis Negative P1
  1. Fill Address Details (Plot/Flat, Street, Area, City, Country, State, District, Pincode) and click '+ Add' - address appears in the address table.
  2. Fill KYC Documents (Document Type=Address Proof, Document Name=Aadhar Card, valid-format Reference Number, Month, Year, uploaded file) and click '+ Add' - document appears in the KYC table.
  3. Click 'Save Contact'.
  4. Verify a success response/navigation occurs and the new contact is findable via search.
 The contact is created successfully once a valid address and KYC document are both present in their summary tables, matching what the UI visually confirms was added. Save Contact is a silent no-op: no network request fires, no success or error message appears, and the contact is not created (confirmed absent via search afterward). Root cause traced to stale 'required' validators left on the Address/KYC entry-row form controls after '+ Add' clears them - the parent form stays invalid indefinitely and Save exits early with no user-facing feedback. Confirmed the same root cause via direct fix: re-populating the Address fields immediately before Save removed them from Angular's invalid-control list, proving the mechanism. See BUG-006 for full technical root cause and recommended fix for the development team. FAIL BUG-006 —

Defect Dashboard

Bug IDTitleModuleSeverityPriorityTest CaseRoot CauseRecommended ResolutionStatus
BUG-001 Unauthenticated users can directly access the post-login branch-selection screen by URL Login / Session Security HIGH P1 TC_LOGIN_SEC02 Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the client-side route guard for #/Userbranchselection does not verify a valid auth token before rendering, or the Angular route resolver fails open when no token is present. Implement/verify a route guard (e.g. Angular CanActivate) on all post-login routes that checks for a valid, server-verified auth token before rendering, and redirect to /Login when absent. Additionally verify equivalent enforcement on backing API endpoints. OPEN
BUG-002 Primary Contact Number field on the Contact form accepts non-numeric characters Contact Management MEDIUM P2 TC_CONTACT_N01 / TC_CONTACT_BV03 / TC_CONTACT_BV05 Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the Primary Contact Number form control only has a minimum-length validator and is missing both a numeric/pattern validator and an exact-length (not just minimum) constraint, e.g. a regex such as ^[0-9]{10}$. Replace the minimum-length-only validator on Primary Contact Number (and Secondary Contact Number) with an exact 10-digit numeric pattern validator (e.g. ^[0-9]{10}$), applied both client-side (Angular reactive form validator) and server-side, and surface a clear 'Contact number must be exactly 10 digits' message. OPEN
BUG-003 Pincode field on the Contact Address form has no format or length validation Contact Management MEDIUM P2 TC_CONTACT_PIN02 / TC_CONTACT_PIN03 / TC_CONTACT_PIN04 Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): no validator is attached to the pPinCode form control at all (neither pattern nor length). Add a 6-digit numeric pattern validator to the Pincode form control (e.g. ^[0-9]{6}$), client-side and server-side, with a clear 'Enter a valid 6-digit pincode' message. OPEN
BUG-004 PAN Card No. field accepts lowercase letters despite enforcing the PAN format otherwise Contact Management LOW P3 TC_CONTACT_PAN03 Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the PAN pattern validator regex uses a case-sensitive character class limited to A-Z and does not also test the lowercase equivalent, and no uppercase-transform is applied on input. Either auto-uppercase PAN input as it is typed (common UX pattern also seen on the Name field in this same form) or make the pattern validator case-insensitive and reject lowercase explicitly with a clear message. OPEN
BUG-005 Primary Email ID format validation does not catch consecutive dots Contact Management LOW P4 TC_CONTACT_EM03 Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the email validation regex does not include a check for consecutive dots in the local part. Low priority - tighten the email validation regex to reject consecutive dots, or adopt a standard RFC 5322-compliant email validator. OPEN
BUG-006 Save Contact silently fails after using "+ Add" on Address Details or KYC Documents - stale required validators block the whole form with zero user feedback Contact Management HIGH P1 Manual verification (see Root Cause Analysis below); not covered by an automated TC_CONTACT_* ID Angular reactive-form required validators remain attached to the transient 'add new row' input controls in the Address Details and KYC Documents sections after their values are committed via '+ Add', and those controls are not excluded from (or re-validated out of) the parent Contact form's overall FormGroup validity. Save Contact appears to gate on parent-form validity with no fallback error UI for this specific case, resulting in a silent no-op. For the dev team - two complementary fixes are recommended: 1. STRUCTURAL FIX (root cause): Move the Address Details and KYC Documents 'add new entry' inputs into their own child FormGroup that is separate from the main Contact FormGroup (e.g. `this.addressEntryForm` / `this.kycEntryForm` rather than nesting `pAddress1` etc. directly under the parent contact form). The parent Save Contact form's validity should be derived from the LENGTH of the committed address/KYC arrays (e.g. `addresses.length > 0`), not from the transient entry-row controls' own validity. This is the standard Angular pattern for 'add to list' UI and will make the bug structurally impossible to reintroduce elsewhere in the app (the same '+ Add' pattern is also used in the Bank Details, Income, and Related Parties tabs, and in the Business Entity form, and should be audited for the same issue). 2. DEFENSIVE FIX (fail loud, not silent): Regardless of the structural fix, the Save Contact button's click handler should never silently no-op. If `contactForm.invalid` is true when Save is clicked, call `markAllAsTouched()` (or equivalent) on the whole form tree and surface a visible summary of which fields/sections are actually invalid, mirroring the existing 'Title Required' / 'Name Required' style toast already used for the top-level fields. This turns any future validator/state bug into a visible, debuggable, user-reportable issue instead of a silent dead end. OPEN
BUG-007 Save on Group Formation form is blocked by a stale "Chit Period Required" validator even when Chit Period holds a valid, ng-valid selection Group Formation HIGH P1 TC_GF_CREATE01 Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed, but consistent with BUG-006's pattern in this codebase): the Group Formation page renders more than one instance of the Chit Period control in the DOM (a duplicate-hidden-component pattern already observed on the Contact Detail/Employee role forms), and the submit-time required check may be reading a different (stale/hidden) FormControl instance than the one the user actually interacted with, or the parent form's cross-field validator recomputes validity from a source that is not kept in sync with the visible control. For the dev team: 1) Audit the Group Formation component for duplicate/hidden instances of the Chit Period (and other) form controls, consistent with the pattern already flagged in BUG-006 for the Contact module - ensure only one FormControl instance backs each visible field. 2) Verify the Save click handler's required-field check reads validity from the same FormGroup instance that data-binds to the visible dropdown, not a stale or duplicate one. 3) As a defensive fix, never let Save silently no-op with zero API calls - call markAllAsTouched() and render a visible, field-specific error summary so a genuine validator/state mismatch is immediately visible and reportable rather than appearing as 'nothing happens'. OPEN

Defect Details

HIGH BUG-001 — Unauthenticated users can directly access the post-login branch-selection screen by URL

ModuleLogin / Session Security
ScreenBranch Selection (#/Userbranchselection)
Test CaseTC_LOGIN_SEC02
PriorityP1
StatusOPEN

Preconditions: Fresh browser session/tab with no prior login and no existing authentication token.

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Open a fresh browser context (no cookies/local storage from a prior session).
  2. Navigate directly to http://host81.kapilits.com:8007/#/Userbranchselection without logging in.
  3. Observe the page that is rendered.

Test Data: N/A - no credentials submitted

Expected ResultThe application should detect the absence of a valid session/auth token and redirect the user back to the Login screen.
Actual ResultThe Branch Selection screen is rendered directly, showing the 'Select Branch' search UI, an account avatar icon in the header, and a Logout link, without requiring authentication.

Evidence:

Root Cause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the client-side route guard for #/Userbranchselection does not verify a valid auth token before rendering, or the Angular route resolver fails open when no token is present.

Recommended Resolution:

Implement/verify a route guard (e.g. Angular CanActivate) on all post-login routes that checks for a valid, server-verified auth token before rendering, and redirect to /Login when absent. Additionally verify equivalent enforcement on backing API endpoints.

MEDIUM BUG-002 — Primary Contact Number field on the Contact form accepts non-numeric characters

ModuleContact Management
ScreenNew Contact - Contact Information (#/configuration/contact)
Test CaseTC_CONTACT_N01 / TC_CONTACT_BV03 / TC_CONTACT_BV05
PriorityP2
StatusOPEN

Preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open (Individual).

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Open Contact > New to load the Individual contact creation form.
  2. In the Primary Contact Number field, enter a 10-character alphabetic string, e.g. 'abcdefghij'.
  3. Move focus to another field (e.g. Father Name) to trigger field-level validation.
  4. Observe whether any validation message appears for the Primary Contact Number field.

Test Data: Primary Contact Number = 'abcdefghij' (10 letters, no digits); also confirmed with '90000000011' (11 digits) and '+919000000001' (leading plus sign)

Expected ResultThe field should be flagged as invalid because it does not contain a plain 10-digit numeric phone number - whether the issue is wrong character class, too many digits, or disallowed symbols.
Actual ResultNo validation message appears for any of the three cases. The field only enforces a MINIMUM fixed length of 10 characters (confirmed separately: a 3-character numeric value correctly triggers 'Enter the data with minimum(10) fixed length'), but has no numeric-only check and no upper bound: an 11-digit number, a value with a leading '+', and a 10-character alphabetic string are all silently accepted.

Evidence:

Root Cause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the Primary Contact Number form control only has a minimum-length validator and is missing both a numeric/pattern validator and an exact-length (not just minimum) constraint, e.g. a regex such as ^[0-9]{10}$.

Recommended Resolution:

Replace the minimum-length-only validator on Primary Contact Number (and Secondary Contact Number) with an exact 10-digit numeric pattern validator (e.g. ^[0-9]{10}$), applied both client-side (Angular reactive form validator) and server-side, and surface a clear 'Contact number must be exactly 10 digits' message.

MEDIUM BUG-003 — Pincode field on the Contact Address form has no format or length validation

ModuleContact Management
ScreenNew Contact - Address Details (#/configuration/contact)
Test CaseTC_CONTACT_PIN02 / TC_CONTACT_PIN03 / TC_CONTACT_PIN04
PriorityP2
StatusOPEN

Preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open, Address Details tab active.

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Open Contact > New, go to the Address Details tab.
  2. Enter 'ABCDEF' (non-numeric) in the Pincode field and move focus away - observe no error.
  3. Enter '12345' (5 digits) in the Pincode field and move focus away - observe no error.
  4. Enter '1234567' (7 digits) in the Pincode field and move focus away - observe no error.

Test Data: Pincode = 'ABCDEF', '12345', '1234567' (a valid Indian pincode is exactly 6 numeric digits)

Expected ResultThe Pincode field should reject non-numeric input and enforce an exact 6-digit length, consistent with Indian postal code format.
Actual ResultNone of the three invalid values (non-numeric, 5-digit, 7-digit) triggered any validation message. The field appears to have no format or length constraint at all, unlike Primary Contact Number, PAN, and Email which each have at least partial validation.

Root Cause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): no validator is attached to the pPinCode form control at all (neither pattern nor length).

Recommended Resolution:

Add a 6-digit numeric pattern validator to the Pincode form control (e.g. ^[0-9]{6}$), client-side and server-side, with a clear 'Enter a valid 6-digit pincode' message.

LOW BUG-004 — PAN Card No. field accepts lowercase letters despite enforcing the PAN format otherwise

ModuleContact Management
ScreenNew Contact - Personal Details (#/configuration/contact)
Test CaseTC_CONTACT_PAN03
PriorityP3
StatusOPEN

Preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open.

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Open Contact > New.
  2. Enter 'abcde1234f' (valid PAN pattern but lowercase) in the PAN Card No. field.
  3. Move focus away and observe whether an 'Invalid PAN Card No.' message appears.

Test Data: PAN Card No. = 'abcde1234f' (compare: 'ABCDE1234F' is accepted; '1234567890' and 'ABC123' are correctly rejected as 'Invalid PAN Card No.')

Expected ResultSince real PAN numbers are always uppercase, a lowercase entry should either be auto-uppercased or rejected as invalid, consistent with the field's own format enforcement for digit/letter placement.
Actual ResultThe lowercase value was accepted with no 'Invalid PAN Card No.' message and no auto-uppercase transformation, even though the field does correctly reject a PAN with the wrong digit/letter pattern.

Root Cause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the PAN pattern validator regex uses a case-sensitive character class limited to A-Z and does not also test the lowercase equivalent, and no uppercase-transform is applied on input.

Recommended Resolution:

Either auto-uppercase PAN input as it is typed (common UX pattern also seen on the Name field in this same form) or make the pattern validator case-insensitive and reject lowercase explicitly with a clear message.

HIGH BUG-006 — Save Contact silently fails after using "+ Add" on Address Details or KYC Documents - stale required validators block the whole form with zero user feedback

ModuleContact Management
ScreenNew Contact - Address Details / KYC Documents (#/configuration/contact)
Test CaseManual verification (see Root Cause Analysis below); not covered by an automated TC_CONTACT_* ID
PriorityP1
StatusOPEN

Preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open (Individual), all top-level mandatory fields filled in (Title, Name, Father Name, Primary Contact Number).

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Fill in the Address Details tab (Plot/Flat No., Street/Building, Area, City/Village, Country, State, District, Pincode) and click '+ Add'. The address correctly appears in the 'Select Primary Address' table below.
  2. Open the KYC Documents tab, select Document Type = 'Address Proof', Document Name = 'Aadhar Card', enter a valid-format Reference Number, Month, Year, and upload a file, then click '+ Add'. The document correctly appears in the 'KYC documents and Income Proof' table below.
  3. Click 'Save Contact'.
  4. Observe: no success message, no error/warning toast, and no network request is sent (confirmed via browser DevTools / Playwright network capture - zero POST calls fire when Save Contact is clicked in this state).
  5. Inspect the Address Details and KYC Documents tabs again: the single-entry input fields (Plot/Flat No., Street/Building, Area, City/Village, Pincode, Document Name, Reference Number, etc.) are empty, exactly as left after step 1/2's '+ Add' cleared them.
  6. Re-populate those same input fields with the same values again (without clicking '+ Add' again) and click 'Save Contact' immediately: the Address-related fields stop blocking the form (confirmed via Angular's .ng-invalid state disappearing for pAddress1/pAddress2/pAddress3/pCity/pPinCode), demonstrating that re-filling the emptied fields is what was missing.

Test Data: Any valid contact data; the defect is structural and reproduces regardless of the specific values entered.

Expected ResultAfter successfully adding an address and a KYC document to their respective lists via '+ Add', the contact record should be created when 'Save Contact' is clicked, since both required pieces of information (address, KYC document) are visibly present in their summary tables. At minimum, if the form is still considered invalid, the user should see a clear message explaining what is missing.
Actual ResultSave Contact is a complete no-op: no API call fires, no message is shown, and the button gives no visual feedback that anything went wrong. The user has no way to know why saving 'does nothing'. Root cause traced (see below): the Address Details and KYC Documents sections are implemented as single reactive-form FormGroups whose individual input controls (pAddress1, pAddress2, pAddress3, pCity, pPinCode for Address; pDocumentGroupId, pDocumentId, pDocReferenceno, pDocumentName for KYC) carry Validators.required. Clicking '+ Add' pushes the current values into a separate list/array for display and visually clears the input row, but does NOT remove or relax the required validators on those now-empty controls, and does NOT exclude that FormGroup from the parent Contact form's overall validity calculation. The parent form therefore remains permanently .invalid after any '+ Add' action, and the Save Contact click handler appears to check the parent form's validity before attempting to submit - so it exits early with no submission and no user-facing error, since the code path that would normally render field-level error messages (as seen for the top-level Personal Details / Contact Information fields) is apparently not wired up for this specific silent-exit case.

Root Cause: Angular reactive-form required validators remain attached to the transient 'add new row' input controls in the Address Details and KYC Documents sections after their values are committed via '+ Add', and those controls are not excluded from (or re-validated out of) the parent Contact form's overall FormGroup validity. Save Contact appears to gate on parent-form validity with no fallback error UI for this specific case, resulting in a silent no-op.

Recommended Resolution:

For the dev team - two complementary fixes are recommended:

1. STRUCTURAL FIX (root cause): Move the Address Details and KYC Documents 'add new entry' inputs into their own child FormGroup that is separate from the main Contact FormGroup (e.g. `this.addressEntryForm` / `this.kycEntryForm` rather than nesting `pAddress1` etc. directly under the parent contact form). The parent Save Contact form's validity should be derived from the LENGTH of the committed address/KYC arrays (e.g. `addresses.length > 0`), not from the transient entry-row controls' own validity. This is the standard Angular pattern for 'add to list' UI and will make the bug structurally impossible to reintroduce elsewhere in the app (the same '+ Add' pattern is also used in the Bank Details, Income, and Related Parties tabs, and in the Business Entity form, and should be audited for the same issue).

2. DEFENSIVE FIX (fail loud, not silent): Regardless of the structural fix, the Save Contact button's click handler should never silently no-op. If `contactForm.invalid` is true when Save is clicked, call `markAllAsTouched()` (or equivalent) on the whole form tree and surface a visible summary of which fields/sections are actually invalid, mirroring the existing 'Title Required' / 'Name Required' style toast already used for the top-level fields. This turns any future validator/state bug into a visible, debuggable, user-reportable issue instead of a silent dead end.

HIGH BUG-007 — Save on Group Formation form is blocked by a stale "Chit Period Required" validator even when Chit Period holds a valid, ng-valid selection

ModuleGroup Formation
ScreenGroup Formation (#/configuration/chitformation)
Test CaseTC_GF_CREATE01
PriorityP1
StatusOPEN

Preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, Group Formation form open.

Steps to Reproduce:

  1. Open Group Formation (#/configuration/chitformation).
  2. Select a valid Chit Value (e.g. '10,000.00-B') from the dropdown.
  3. Select a valid Chit Period (e.g. '12 Months') from the dropdown - confirmed the control's own CSS class list shows 'ng-valid' immediately after selection, i.e. Angular considers this single control valid in isolation.
  4. Fill No. of Auctions, a unique Chit Group Code, and Maximum Subscription with valid values.
  5. Click 'Save'.
  6. Observe the page: 'Chit Period Required' (and, separately, 'Auction Date Required' if the auction date/week toggle was not completed) is shown, and zero non-GET API calls are fired.

Test Data: Chit Value='B' (10,000.00-B), Chit Period='X1-12' (12 Months), No. of Auctions='12', Chit Group Code=synthetic unique value 'QATESTnnnnnn', Maximum Subscription='1'

Expected ResultSince Chit Period holds a valid selection (confirmed via the control's own ng-valid state), submitting the form should not report 'Chit Period Required'; Save should proceed to call the save API (or report only the fields that are genuinely still empty, e.g. Auction Date).
Actual Result'Chit Period Required' is shown and Save fires zero API calls, even though the visible/active Chit Period control's own class list is 'ng-valid ng-dirty ng-untouched' at the moment of submission. This is the same class of defect as BUG-006 on the Contact form: a required-field check that does not agree with the individual control's own validity state, resulting in a silent block with no way for the user to know Chit Period is the (apparently mistaken) blocker.

Root Cause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed, but consistent with BUG-006's pattern in this codebase): the Group Formation page renders more than one instance of the Chit Period control in the DOM (a duplicate-hidden-component pattern already observed on the Contact Detail/Employee role forms), and the submit-time required check may be reading a different (stale/hidden) FormControl instance than the one the user actually interacted with, or the parent form's cross-field validator recomputes validity from a source that is not kept in sync with the visible control.

Recommended Resolution:

For the dev team: 1) Audit the Group Formation component for duplicate/hidden instances of the Chit Period (and other) form controls, consistent with the pattern already flagged in BUG-006 for the Contact module - ensure only one FormControl instance backs each visible field. 2) Verify the Save click handler's required-field check reads validity from the same FormGroup instance that data-binds to the visible dropdown, not a stale or duplicate one. 3) As a defensive fix, never let Save silently no-op with zero API calls - call markAllAsTouched() and render a visible, field-specific error summary so a genuine validator/state mismatch is immediately visible and reportable rather than appearing as 'nothing happens'.
